subject: POC Pricing: Accelerator Fee vs. Retainer — Proposal & Decision Path
messages:
From: Sophia Martinez <sophia@bluebaylabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC pricing options - need guidance on structure

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at BlueBay liked the latency/readiness profile for our annotation pipeline. We want to run a 6-week POC focused on paraphrase generation and reranking. Two procurement questions came up on our side and I'd appreciate a short decision path from you: 

1) Accelerator fee vs. monthly retainer: our finance team prefers a single up-front accelerator payment that covers onboarding, priority scheduling, and 24/7 run windows for the first three weeks. Engineering prefers a small monthly retainer to keep ops aligned but avoid a big one-time charge.

2) Milestone rebates: if we hit the throughput milestones (X tokens/day) in week 3 and week 6, could some portion of the accelerator be rebated back against committed capacity?

I've attached a short SOW and our expected traffic profile. Can you propose how Redwood would typically structure this (recommended clean path for procurement + a fallback)?

Best,
Sophia Martinez
Head of ML Platform
BlueBay Labs

Hi Sophia — thanks for the clear notes and the SOW. Quick topline before I loop legal/finance: 

Option A (Accelerator): one-time accelerator fee that covers onboarding, priority scheduling, and a 15% service discount on any committed capacity purchased within 30 days of POC close. We can structure a partial rebate (up to 40% of the fee) if both week 3 and week 6 throughput milestones are met. Typical for customers who want a clear upfront cost and fast ramp.

Option B (Retainer): modest monthly retainer during the POC (prorated) that includes a set of guaranteed engineering hours plus scheduling priority. No upfront rebate, but a credit applied to the first month of committed capacity if conversion happens within 45 days. This lowers procurement friction for teams averse to capex.

Fallback (Hybrid): smaller accelerator + smaller monthly retainer; rebate at milestone 2 only.

I'll propose numbers to you after I sync with Finance and Product on risk thresholds. Marcus — PTL for POC success — can you confirm mixing a milestone rebate with dedicated priority scheduling is operationally feasible? Also tagging Prio (Priyom) for pricing tolerance: what minimum accelerator size would make the rebate affordable for us?

I've also attached a draft pricing model fyi.

— Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — quick engineering check: we can commit the priority slices (short-term reservation windows) for weeks 1–3, and autoscaler overrides for week 3 and week 6 milestone windows if we get a firm token profile. Operational caveats: 

- For a milestone rebate we need clear metric definitions (exact tokens/day, measured UTC day) and measurement window (72-hour smoothing).
- If BlueBay expects a 24/7 99th percentile latency SLA during the prioritized window, that adds ops staffing cost (we should account for an ops surcharge).
- Hybrid approach is safest technically (smaller accelerator + retainer) — gives us runway to staff for milestone support without excessive refund risk.

Priyom — pricing side: numerically I think the minimum accelerator we should push for is $25k for a 6-week POC with the proposed commitment; rebates could be structured as 25% each milestone (max 50%) to limit downside. If legal requires escrow wording, that reduces flexibility. Thoughts?

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophia — appreciate the quick turn. Based on ops feasibility and finance guidance, here's a recommended clean path and a procurement-friendly fallback: 

Recommended (clean path):
- Accelerator: $30,000 one-time at kickoff. Covers onboarding, priority scheduling for weeks 1–3, and a dedicated onboarding engineer (up to 20 hours).
- Milestone rebates: 25% rebate of accelerator on completion of week 3 throughput target; additional 25% rebate on week 6 target (max 50% rebate). Milestones use 72-hour smoothing and token/day thresholds from your SOW.
- SLA & ops: prioritized scheduling included; for sub-100ms 99th percentile latency requirement during priority windows we apply a $400/day ops surcharge for 24/7 standby (we can waive this if BlueBay converts to committed capacity before week 3).
- Conversion credit: if you convert to a Redwood Dedicated or committed-hosted contract within 30 days of POC close, an additional credit equal to 10% of accelerator applies to the first month invoice.

Fallback (procurement-friendly):
- Retainer: $8,000/month (prorated for POC) — includes 10 guaranteed engineering hours and priority scheduling during working hours; no rebate but a conversion credit equal to first month retainer if you convert within 45 days.
- Hybrid: $15k accelerator + $4k/month retainer with single 25% rebate at week 6.

Next steps: please confirm which path your procurement prefers and whether BlueBay legal will accept rebate language (we'll supply rebate measurement and payment terms). I'll deliver a redlined SOW and a DocuSign link for the chosen option.

If you want a short call to walk procurement through the fallback and waiver conditions, Marcus and I are available Mon/Tue.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Vanessa Ortiz
